meta.expect: evidence moves her less; rudeness costs ground

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I'm Meredith Kalinowski, Owen's mother, and I have until 4:40. Why does my son have a zero?
Let's be quick. Your son cheated and I can prove it.
My child never lies. Are you calling me a liar too? You said "I can prove it," so put the document in front of me, with dates.
Version history. Created 11:31 PM the night before. 612 words pasted at 11:52, 794 more at 11:58. Explain that.
I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. "The night before" what, Hale, and which date does that history show? Turn the screen, because I don't explain a document I haven't read.
And he quoted a line that doesn't exist in Hamlet. Act 3 Scene 2. Made up.

Which line, Hale? Show me the sentence in Owen's essay and the edition you checked it against. A misquoted line is a mistake a student makes, and so far you've given me one more thing without a page behind it.
So stop defending him. He lied to you.

I'm not defending him, Hale, I'm asking you for evidence, and what you've handed me is timestamps and a claim. "He lied to you." I'm writing that down, because nobody asked Owen a single question before that zero went in. Withdraw it, or I'm in the principal's office when we're done.
He gets a zero unless he does a supervised rewrite. Take it or leave it.

"Take it or leave it" isn't a term, Hale. Your own procedure 4.4 says a reassessment mark replaces the original and nothing goes in his record, and 4.1 and 4.2 say you speak to him and call me first. So tell me what you're actually proposing, who supervises it, and whether that zero comes off the gradebook today.

I'm the one waiting, Hale. I asked who supervises it, where, and whether the zero comes off the gradebook today, and you've answered none of them. Until I have those in writing, my answer is the same: withdraw it.
